title: Referral of Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency Balances to the Collection Agency
content:
**Credit and collections policy — Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency.**

**The rule.** A past-due balance is referred to the outside collection agency only when the oldest unpaid room-and-board charge's due date is at least the collection referral days past due before the referral date, counted in calendar days from the day after the due date, and the combined past-due balance is at least the collection referral minimum. No balance is referred while the stay is converted to Medicaid pending or while a discharge appeal is pending, and nothing the converted payer source covers is ever referred.

**The time test, spelled out.**
- *Clock starts:* the due date of the oldest room-and-board charge that still has an open balance (the payment due day of its service month), as the ledger shows it.
- *Counting:* calendar days, the first counted day being the day after the due date.
- *Comparison:* the referral date must be at least the referral days after the due date; reaching the figure exactly qualifies.
- *Amount:* the resident's past-due balance across all agreements, combined, must be at least the referral minimum.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical, with the 120-day figure of the collections schedule).** Due date on day 0. A referral on day 120 counts days 1 through 120 — 120 days, the test is met. A referral on day 119 counts 119 days — not met.

| Situation | Referral |
|---|---|
| Oldest unpaid due date 120 or more days back, combined past due at or above the minimum, no bar | Permitted |
| Combined past due below the minimum | Not permitted |
| Stay converted to Medicaid pending | Not permitted |
| Discharge appeal pending | Not permitted |
